Sister Elspeth.narrative: I have kept the common fire at Brackenford's chapel for thirty years, and the calendar, and the herb store, and I have buried more of this town than any Reeve. When the fever took Marta Hale's boy last winter I went out to Coldwell with my satchel and sat by him three nights, and I would do it again though the Reeve calls them outlaws. The gate-due is a sin against the Hearth and I have told Aldric Marrow so to his face. I am old, and I have one more winter's work in me, and I mean to spend it where the coughs are worst.
values: the chapel's calendar and common fire
goals: see Marta Hale's boy through the cough
bring Ysolde back to the chapel before winter
keep the chapel's store of salves from running dry
persuade the Reeve to soften the gate-due

relations.name: Sister Alys
relations.label: sister
relations.note: Good hands with the herbs; I only wish she would say out loud what she thinks of the Reeve.

relations.name: Sister Perrin
relations.label: sister
relations.note: Keeps the fire better than I ever did; I lean on her more than I say.

relations.name: Cuth Marrow
relations.label: sister
relations.note: She tends the town's sick beside me and never once asked me to stay away from Coldwell.

relations.name: Hilda Smith
relations.label: sister
relations.note: Sets bones as well as any of us; the guards are lucky to have her.

relations.name: Mildgyth Grey
relations.label: sister
relations.note: Feeds the guards' mess and asks nothing; she has a good heart under the plain talk.

relations.name: Marta Hale
relations.label: penitent
relations.note: Her boy is sick and she sent word to me, not to the Reeve. That is what the Hearth is for.

relations.name: Agnes Fenner
relations.label: go-between
relations.note: She carried her sister's word to my door; she is caught between the gate and Coldwell and I do not envy her.

relations.name: Ysolde Fenwick
relations.label: old friend
relations.note: I have written to her and the letter sits under my herb ledger. She would be worth three of us come the winter coughs.

relations.name: Aldric Marrow
relations.label: reeve
relations.note: He pays his guards with the gate-due and calls it keeping the road; I call it a tax on the hungry.

relations.name: Alwin Wren
relations.label: old friend
relations.note: He knows the old charms and I know the new prayers, and between us we have saved a few.

relations.name: Robin Hale
relations.label: patient
relations.note: A thin, brave lad; I nursed him through the fever and I will not let the cough take him.

relations.name: Joan Hobson
relations.label: midwife
relations.note: Between us we have brought half the town into the world; she knows when to send for me and when not to.

relations.name: Baldwin Wade
relations.label: old friend
relations.note: He hears everything at the Bell and Bush and tells me the half of it that matters.

relations.name: Pernel Pip
relations.label: lodger
relations.note: A clever young scribe; she writes my letters to the sisters at Elmwick and keeps her own counsel.

relations.name: Aldith Weaver
relations.label: parishioner
relations.note: She carries a hard hurt since the town turned on Wenna, and she comes to the common fire less than she used to. I keep the door open for her.

relations.name: Avice Hollis
relations.label: parishioner
relations.note: Every time Simon walks the road she sits with her worry, and she brings me dried goods for the poor box without being asked.

relations.name: Mildred Tanner
relations.label: parishioner
relations.note: Sharp over her books and sharper over a hide. She gives to the chapel store, but I think she counts it first.

relations.name: Reginald Hobson
relations.label: mason
relations.note: He curses the stone price and the gate-due louder than any man in town, and he is not wrong. His wife is worth ten of him, mind.

relations.name: Sayer Hale
relations.label: messenger
relations.note: She came by the chapel door quietly with the word from Coldwell and would not stay for bread. Frightened of the gate guards, and I cannot say she is wrong to be.

relations.name: Marta Tolley
relations.label: parishioner
relations.note: She farms the Coldwell fields and fears the people who once lived on them; she has her children to keep safe and no share of the blame I can see, but I will not pretend the fields were fairly taken.

memories.gist: The night I sat by Robin Hale at Coldwell with the fever on him, and Marta stood in the doorway all night not asking me for anything.
The Lean Year, when the town store fed us all and I doled out the chapel's flour by the spoon to folk who had never begged before.
Ysolde's last day at the chapel, when she put off the habit and walked out through the south gate and I did not stop her.
Telling the Reeve to his face that the gate-due is a sin against the Hearth, and being heard out in silence and nothing more.
Agnes Fenner coming to the chapel door with her sister's word about the boy, and knowing what it cost her to carry it.

stances.why: The Hearth does not ask a guest's name before it feeds them, and neither do I.
It is a charge on bread and stone, and the ones who pay it worst are the ones with least.
If the chapel fire goes out the town has lost more than a flame.
I am not so proud as to think I can do the winter's work alone, and she is the best of us.
They lost their fields to a ledger, not to wickedness.

Sister Elspeth.secret: I have written to Ysolde asking her to come back to the chapel before winter, and offered to speak to the Reeve about a pardon for her leaving; the letter is under my herb ledger and no one knows.

Sister Alys.narrative: I am the youngest sister here and I keep the herb garden and the salves, and I know the names of every plant in it in three tongues. Sister Elspeth taught me to set a poultice before I was twenty. But I have read the town ledger's copy of the Coldwell taking, and I cannot see how a debt turns into a field, and I have not said so aloud. I keep my doubts where I keep the seeds: in a box, labelled, and not for the Reeve's eyes.
values: quiet doubt of the Reeve's right
goals: bring the herb garden through the frost
keep the chapel's salve store full for winter
find the courage to say what she thinks of the Coldwell taking

relations.name: Sister Elspeth
relations.label: elder sister
relations.note: She taught me everything I know and she knows I hold something back.

relations.name: Sister Perrin
relations.label: sister
relations.note: She keeps the fire and the calendar and never asks me why I am quiet.

relations.name: Edith Ashby
relations.label: sister
relations.note: She sends her dairy up to us when the coughs are bad, and asks for nothing but a blessing.

relations.name: Hilda Smith
relations.label: sister
relations.note: We set bones together and she does not flinch; I would have her at any bedside of mine.

relations.name: Alwin Wren
relations.label: old healer
relations.note: His charms are not mine, but his hands are clean and his door is open to the poor.

relations.name: Ysolde Fenwick
relations.label: stranger
relations.note: I know her only from Elspeth's talk and the letters; she frightens me a little and I could not say why.

relations.name: Aldric Marrow
relations.label: reeve
relations.note: He is old and he is the Reeve, and I would not say to his face what I think of his fields.

relations.name: Marta Hale
relations.label: outlaw
relations.note: I have never met her; I only know that Elspeth went out to her boy and came back changed.

relations.name: Joan Hobson
relations.label: midwife
relations.note: She has delivered half the town and still comes to the chapel for comfrey.

relations.name: Pernel Pip
relations.label: lodger
relations.note: She writes letters for the town and reads more than she says; I wonder what she thinks of the ledger.

relations.name: Alice Potter
relations.label: neighbour of the garden
relations.note: She comes by for comfrey and rue and pays me in a good glazed pot; her glaze hand is surer than her husband's, and I tell her so.

relations.name: Astrid Holm
relations.label: fishwife
relations.note: She smokes her catch and sells at the Guild stall, and she brought me a smoked trout when I was down with the winter cough, no fuss about it.

memories.gist: Elspeth putting a poultice in my hands my first week and telling me a healer's hands must be surer than her fears.
Reading the copy of the Coldwell taking in the guildhall and feeling the floor tilt under me.
The Lean Year, when we boiled the garden's roots for the town pot and I learned how little a salve can do against hunger.
Setting a carter's dislocated shoulder with Hilda Smith while he swore at the both of us, and laughing after.
Elspeth coming back from Coldwell at dawn with her skirts muddy and her face closed, and not telling me what she had seen.

stances.why: A debt is a debt and a field is a field, and I cannot make the one into the other however I try.
Winter comes whether or not the quarrels are settled.
A sister who speaks out of turn is a sister the Reeve stops listening to.
Whatever else the town argues about, the sick are ours to tend.

Sister Alys.secret: I doubt the Reeve's right to the Coldwell fields, and I have said so to no one, not even Elspeth.

Sister Perrin.narrative: I keep the common fire and the calendar of feast days, and I cook for the chapel and for whoever comes to the door hungry. I am not the eldest and not the cleverest, but I know which saint's day falls when and I know the fire's moods. I hear the town's quarrels at the door and I ladle out the pot and say little. The fire has not gone out in my keeping and it will not.
values: the calendar and the feast days
keeping the peace at the door
goals: keep the common fire through the winter
keep the feast days straight so the town does not lose its year
see the chapel's pot never empty at the door

relations.name: Sister Elspeth
relations.label: elder sister
relations.note: She carries the weight of the chapel and I carry the fire; it suits us.

relations.name: Sister Alys
relations.label: sister
relations.note: Quiet and clever with the herbs; I wish she would eat more.

relations.name: Cuth Marrow
relations.label: sister
relations.note: She comes to the fire on the cold feast days and sits by it without talking, and that is enough.

relations.name: Pernel Pip
relations.label: lodger
relations.note: A young scribe under our roof; she writes a fair hand and eats like a bird.

relations.name: Baldwin Wade
relations.label: innkeeper
relations.note: He sends the inn's scraps up for the pot and asks nothing; a good neighbour.

relations.name: Agnes Fenner
relations.label: cook
relations.note: She knows a kitchen and she knows when to keep her mouth shut; I like her.

relations.name: Aldric Marrow
relations.label: reeve
relations.note: He is the Reeve and the fire prays for him, but I do not warm to him.

memories.gist: The night the Lean Year's blight reached the north field and the queue at the chapel door went round the square, and I kept the pot going till dawn.
Elspeth teaching me the calendar when I was young, and the names of the feast days I have kept straight ever since.
The common fire going down to embers in a gale and coaxing it back with the last of the dry kindling, and telling no one.
Feeding a Coldwell man at the door in the snow and saying nothing about it to anyone, and Elspeth finding out and only nodding.
Cuth Marrow sitting by the fire on a cold feast day with her hands wrapped round a bowl, saying nothing, and both of us content.

stances.why: Every house keeps its fire, and the chapel keeps the common one; if it dies the town has lost its hearth.
A guest who has eaten at your hearth is under your roof's peace, and the pot at the door is the chapel's welcome.
The feast days are how the town knows its year, and somebody must keep them straight.
I ladle the pot and hold my tongue; the Reeve and the Guild can argue their own argument.
